records.notes: The visible lexical form is consistent; editions differ in initial alif/wasla, dagger-alif, and stopping-mark presentation.
Visible forms differ as حَيَّ, حَـِۧيَ, and حَيِيَ across the editions, showing distinct letter/vowel realization rather than a simple stopping mark.
Visible forms differ in initial alif/wasla, hamza, dagger-alif, and vowel presentation in الفئتان; the evidence does not support a confident semantic subtype.
Visible forms show يَحۡسَبَنَّ in Hafs, تَحۡسَبَنَّ in Shu'bah, and تَحۡسِبَنَّ in the other editions, with clear initial and vowel differences.
Visible forms show ٱلنَّبِيُّ or اَ۬لنَّبِيُّ in most editions and اَ۬لنَّبِےٓءُ in Warsh/Qalun, a clear final hamza/letter-form difference.
